chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Abi Hilal al-Madainy, from Hadeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, when the servant supplicates, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the two angels: 'I have answered him, but withhold his need, for I love to hear his voice.' And when the servant supplicates, Allah, Blessed and High, says: 'Hasten his need for him, for I dislike hearing his voice.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah delay answering some prayers while hastening others?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the timing of answered supplications, distinguishing between delay as an act of affection and haste as a form of relief. It highlights the concept of 'Istijabah' (answering) not merely as the granting of the request, but as the spiritual intimacy derived from the servant's continuous invocation. This perspective encourages believers to view delays in dua not as rejection, but as an opportunity for deeper connection with the Divine.
